sources.name: Story events, every one of the night
Count trails and our forecast margins

note: Built by scripts/build_retro.py from the board's own files after the night. Chances are 0 to 1, for the Democratic side (the independent in Nebraska, Montana, Idaho and South Dakota). Margins are that side's lead in points of all votes. Calls are CNN's (AP) or Wikipedia's. A call seen only on the backup AP feed counts as uncalled until one of them carried it. Counts were still moving when this was built.

field_labels.note: pre_d, our_line, chance and control_path are the board's own model numbers, read from its files. Everything else inferred is computed here.

senate.control_rule: Democrats need 51 seats, counting King and Sanders, the two independents who caucus with them. Republicans need 50, since the vice president breaks ties.

moments.title: The first polls closed, in Indiana and Kentucky.
moments.body: The last poll closing on the board came at 12:00am, in Alaska.

moments.title: The first votes were counted, in the KY-5 House race.
moments.body: 4,292 votes at 6:03pm.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate jumped from 56% to 96%.
moments.body: Democrats' chance to win the Senate passed 75% and 95% for the first time. Democrats' chance to win the House passed 95% and 99% for the first time. What moved it: the count moving across many Senate races at once. It did not hold: 72% by 7:41pm. The model was changed at 7:22pm, since one state's early count was moving every race too much.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate dropped from 94% to 77%.
moments.body: It did not hold: 96% by 7:34pm. The model was changed at 7:22pm, since one state's early count was moving every race too much.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate jumped from 75% to 96%.
moments.body: What moved it: the count moving across many Senate races at once. It did not hold: 69% by 7:51pm. The model was changed at 7:44pm: since then the live chances read the national swing only from states with half their vote counted.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate dropped from 91% to 72%.
moments.body: The model was changed at 7:44pm: since then the live chances read the national swing only from states with half their vote counted.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the House reached 95% and stayed there.
moments.body: By then 7 of 35 Senate races and 41 of 435 House races had been called.

moments.title: Cooper (D) won the North Carolina Senate race, a seat Republicans held.
moments.body: Called at 8:29pm. Our forecast gave Cooper 96%.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate jumped from 69% to 87%.
moments.body: It did not hold: 74% by 8:54pm. The biggest race move then: Kansas Senate, from 42% to 63% for the Democratic side.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate reached 95% and stayed there.
moments.body: By then 16 of 35 Senate races and 134 of 435 House races had been called.

moments.title: Upset in the South Carolina Senate race: Andrews (D) won with 13% in our forecast.
moments.body: Called at 10:02pm. Andrews first led at 7:26pm.

moments.title: Democrats' chance to win the Senate passed 99% for the first time.
moments.body: By then 17 of 35 Senate races and 177 of 435 House races had been called.

moments.body: Called at 10:55pm. Our forecast gave Talarico 52%.

moments.title: The last polls on the board closed, in Alaska.
moments.body: 178 of the 506 Senate, governor and House races were still uncalled then.

shifts.label: inferred
shifts.basis: Each county's 2026 margin minus its 2024 presidential margin, in points, from CNN's county results (AP's numbers) for both years, read 2026-11-04T09:11:32-05:00. One race per state: the Senate race, else the governor race, with a Democrat on the ballot. Counties at least 90% counted: 2417. Left out: 237 counties under 90% counted, the city election boards Illinois reports beside their counties, the town results of CT, MA, ME, NH, RI, VT, Alaska's 41 districts (drawn differently in 2024), and MT (only an independent on the Democratic side). Kinds cover the board's key counties: 78 of 99 are in (10 counted by town, 6 no statewide race, 5 under 90% counted). The weighted shift weights each county by its 2026 votes. A Senate or governor candidate is not a presidential one, so part of each shift is the candidates.
